import copy
original = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
shallow = copy.copy(original)
shallow[0].append(99)

What happens to original after this?
choices: original is unchanged - shallow is completely independent
original[0] now also contains 99 - shallow only copied the outer list, so the inner lists are still shared
This raises a TypeError, since lists can't be shallow-copied
explanation: A shallow copy duplicates the OUTER container but keeps references to the SAME inner objects - shallow and original point to different outer lists, but shallow[0] and original[0] are still the exact same inner list, so mutating one shows up in the other. copy.deepcopy() would avoid this by recursively copying everything.
